title: Hemispheric failforward policy with capacity throttles and latency-aware fallthrough
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a hemisphere-aware request routing policy that prefers local-region capacity but can 'failforward' to the paired hemisphere when local latency SLOs or capacity constraints are breached. This feature combines latency-based routing, geo pinning heuristics, capacity-aware steering, and adaptive circuit-breakers to minimize user-visible latency and avoid large-scale head-of-line congestion.

Scope:
- Define hemisphere affinity (primary/secondary pairs) and region weights.
- Latency SLOs: per-tenant 95p generation latency target and global 99p alerting thresholds.
- Capacity signals: GPU pool utilization, queue depth, tail-latency heatmap, and per-model concurrency reservations.
- Circuit-breaker modes: probe, open, half-open with exponential backoff and probe traffic to validate recovery.
- Failforward semantics: when local region is in open circuit or trending toward SLO breach, traffic is gradually shifted to hemisphere partner with budgeted percentages and rollback window.
- Geo pinning: sticky routing for session affinity but should support TTL-based pin eviction when capacity pressure mandates migration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulated traffic run (traffic-perf harness) demonstrates <3% user requests sent to >200ms extra network RTT regions under steady-state.
- Under synthetic local capacity saturation test, failforward shifts up to 40% traffic within 30s and stabilizes without triggering global overload.
- Circuit-breaker transitions logged and surfaced in Console; traces link to request IDs and region decisions.
- Integration tests for half-open probing behavior and graceful rollback completed.

Out-of-scope: fine-grained per-customer monetary cost-rebalancing and custom tenant routing policies (separate follow-up).
comments: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: Design sketch completed. Decided on hemisphere pairing approach instead of full mesh to simplify capacity accounting. See design note: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RR/Hemispheric+Failforward+Design

2026-03-02 - Engineering review: Sizing suggestion from infra: add a dedicated short-lived probe queue to avoid contending with normal requests during half-open checks. Action: Miguel to prototype probe queue (ENG-PR-2031).
2026-03-04 - PM feedback (Jordan Ellis): request to include per-customer opt-out for automatic failforward for compliance customers. Marked as dependency on PM/priv-deploy checklist.

2026-03-06 - Spike results: initial simulation shows risk of oscillation when TTL for pinning is <60s under flapping capacity. We propose hysteresis window of 90s and a damping factor for re-pinning. Attach sim dashboard: https://dd.redwood.ai/dashboards/sim-hemispheric-128765
2026-03-09 - Security check: Confirmed no additional data plane changes; control plane rollout requires audit logging flags enabled for private deployments. Security reviewer: Mei Zhang.

2026-03-12 - Implementation: Prototype implemented in request-router v2 branch. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/request-router/pull/842. Unit tests for circuit-breaker state machine added. Pending load test in staging.
